east_africa_presence: SOSUMO operates Burundi's only sugar factory and sugarcane plantations in the Moso region, supplying the domestic sugar market.
expansion_signal: Burundi's Council of Ministers reviewed and endorsed progress on SOSUMO's rehabilitation, modernization and extension project (roadmap approved June 9, 2021), aimed at expanding milling capacity contingent on securing sugarcane supply.
source_title: The SOSUMO rehabilitation, modernization and extension project is reaching a satisfactory stage

company: Axian Telecom (Yas Comoros / Telecom Comores SA)
east_africa_presence: Axian Telecom, via its Comoros subsidiary Telecom Comores SA (branded Yas Comoros), is the country's second mobile network operator, providing mobile, fixed broadband and mobile-money services across the archipelago.
expansion_signal: IFC approved (Dec 17, 2024) and signed (May 30, 2025) a senior secured loan of up to €25M (~US$27M) to Telecom Comores SA to fund capital expenditure and a 2024-2026 mobile network expansion program, including 5G and fibre-to-the-home/office rollout, disbursed October 10, 2025.
source_title: 49849 - Axian Comoros II & Tanzania

east_africa_presence: Following MSC's acquisition of Bolloré Africa Logistics, Africa Global Logistics operates freight-forwarding, dry-port and transport logistics infrastructure in DRC.
expansion_signal: MSC completed its $6.1 billion acquisition of Bolloré Africa Logistics, covering its DRC logistics operations, on 21 December 2022.
source_title: MSC Completes Acquisition of Bolloré Africa Logistics

company: Saudi Ajyal Petroleum and Energy Company
east_africa_presence: Saudi Ajyal is developing a large-scale oil refinery in the Djibouti Damerjog International Park (DDIP), positioned to serve regional Horn of Africa fuel demand.
expansion_signal: Cornerstone for a 300,000 barrels-per-day refinery on 300 hectares in DDIP was laid in June 2024, expected to create roughly 10,000 direct jobs.
source_title: Saudi Arabia expands footprint in Djibouti with major investment projects

east_africa_presence: PAIX is entering Djibouti to build a cloud- and carrier-neutral data centre leveraging Djibouti's position as a landing point for roughly ten undersea cables.
expansion_signal: PAIX signed a joint-venture/MOU with the Djibouti Sovereign Wealth Fund (announced May 16, 2024) to build a ~50,000 sq ft, up to 5MW data centre, with the first phase expected to open in 2026.
source_title: PAIX to Construct Carrier-neutral Data Center in Djibouti

company: China Merchants Port Holdings Company Limited
east_africa_presence: China Merchants holds a 23.5% stake in the Port of Djibouti and is a key investor/co-developer in the Djibouti International Free Trade Zone (DIFTZ).
expansion_signal: China Merchants signed a deal on January 8, 2021 to fund a $3 billion expansion of Djibouti City port and DIFTZ, building on an initial $513 million phase that began October 8, 2020.
source_title: China Merchants signs deal for $3bn expansion of Djibouti City port

east_africa_presence: Sichuan Road and Bridge Group acquired Australian miner Danakali's 50% stake in the Colluli potash project in Eritrea.
expansion_signal: Sichuan Road and Bridge Group completed its purchase of Danakali's 50% Colluli potash project stake, with a first $105 million instalment paid by 31 March 2023.
investment_as_disclosed: US$105 million (first instalment) plus a further US$16 million tranche
source_title: Danakali sells stake in flagship Colluli potash project in Eritrea

east_africa_presence: Building Ethiopia's first JCI-accredited, 350-bed multispecialty hospital in Addis Ababa, positioned as the anchor of a planned African medical-tourism hub.
expansion_signal: Received first $42M equity tranche (of a $130M Phase 1) to fund construction of Roha Medical Campus hospital near Bole International Airport; announced February 22, 2024.
source_title: Roha Medical Campus, a World-Class Hospital in Ethiopia, Gets $42 Million First Injection

east_africa_presence: Africa's largest airline/cargo group, operating from its Bole hub with a continent-wide freight network.
expansion_signal: Opened a new $55M e-commerce/cargo sorting hub at Bole International Airport built to serve Alibaba and Shein, with 150,000-tonne annual capacity; inaugurated February 29, 2024.
source_title: Ethiopian Airlines Opens $55 Million Cargo Center At Addis Ababa Airport

company: Komari Beverage (Arada) — acquired by Heineken N.V.
hq: Amhara Region, Ethiopia (parent: Heineken N.V., Amsterdam, Netherlands)
east_africa_presence: Heineken has operated breweries in Ethiopia since 2011 (Kilinto, Harar, Bedele) as part of a EUR310M+ cumulative investment, and diversified via acquisition into the local spirits/hard-seltzer category.
expansion_signal: Acquired ownership of the Arada hard-seltzer brand from Ethiopian producer Komari Beverage (which built a $29M+ factory in Amhara region); deal concluded mid-October 2024.
source_title: Heineken acquires Komari Beverage

east_africa_presence: Pan-African data centre operator (Uganda, DRC, Mozambique, Cote d'Ivoire) that entered Ethiopia with its flagship East African facility.
expansion_signal: Launched ET1, a Tier III, 3MW/800-rack data centre in Addis Ababa's Ethio ICT Park; opened November 2023.
source_title: Raxio launches data center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

east_africa_presence: Longtime Ethiopian infrastructure contractor (Addis Ababa-Djibouti railway, Hawassa & Dire Dawa industrial parks, Modjo dry port expansion); now building a new special economic zone.
expansion_signal: Broke ground on the Lume Free Trade Zone within the new Gada Special Economic Zone in Oromia (~65km SE of Addis Ababa), Ethiopia's second free trade zone; groundbreaking May 10, 2024.
source_title: Ethiopia launches construction of Chinese-contracted economic zone

east_africa_presence: Amsons Group is a Tanzanian family-owned conglomerate active in cement, bulk petroleum, wheat milling and LPG across Tanzania, Burundi, DR Congo, Mozambique and Zambia, generating over $1 billion in annual turnover; its Kenyan subsidiary Amsons Industries (K) Ltd is moving to take control of Bamburi Cement, Kenya's largest cement producer.
expansion_signal: Launched a mandatory buyout offer for all shares of Bamburi Cement Plc at KSh65/share (a 44% premium), a deal valued at roughly KSh 23.59 billion, to acquire Holcim's 58.6% stake and delist Bamburi from the Nairobi Securities Exchange; announced July 15, 2024.
source_title: Inside Amsons Group's KShs 23.59bn Buyout Offer for Bamburi Cement

east_africa_presence: Major Kenyan industrial conglomerate producing cement and steel, with operations spanning Kenya, Uganda, DRC, Rwanda and Zambia.
expansion_signal: Launched the Cemtech Sebit Clinkerization Plant in West Pokot on April 8, 2024 - a 2-million-tonne-per-year clinker facility ending Kenya's reliance on imported clinker.
source_title: Devki Opens Sh29bn Clinker Factory in West Pokot

hq: Redmond, USA (partner G42 HQ'd in Abu Dhabi, UAE)
east_africa_presence: Establishing Kenya as its flagship East African digital hub, including a new Azure cloud region and an Innovation Lab in Nairobi.
expansion_signal: Announced (with G42) a $1 billion comprehensive digital ecosystem initiative on May 22, 2024, including a geothermal-powered data centre in Olkaria and a new Azure East Africa Cloud Region.
source_title: Microsoft and G42 announce $1 billion comprehensive digital ecosystem initiative for Kenya

east_africa_presence: Huawei has operated in Kenya for over two decades, partnering with the Kenyan government on national ICT infrastructure, most notably building the Konza Technopolis National Cloud Data Centre and Government Cloud alongside network infrastructure for local telecom operators.
expansion_signal: Committed to build a National Cloud data centre, smart ICT/surveillance systems and a Government Cloud at Konza Technopolis, financed via Chinese concessional loans; Phase 1 (containerized National Data Centre) completed July 2020, valued at KSh 17.5 billion.
source_title: Phase One National Data Center at Konza Completed

east_africa_presence: Operates a Nairobi-based Development Centre - AWS's second in Africa after Cape Town - housing R&D, cloud support and software engineering teams.
expansion_signal: Launched its second African Development Centre on Riverside Drive, Nairobi, October 5, 2023.
source_title: AWS Launches its second African Development Centre in Kenya

east_africa_presence: Energy Fuels is advancing the Toliara Project in southwestern Madagascar, a titanium, zirconium and rare-earth mineral sands project.
expansion_signal: Energy Fuels and the Government of Madagascar executed an MOU on 5 December 2024 to further advance the Toliara project toward a final investment decision.
investment_as_disclosed: Multi-billion-dollar project potential; ~US$80 million committed to development/community/social funding
source_title: Energy Fuels and Madagascar Government Execute Memorandum of Understanding to Further Advance Toliara Critical Mineral Project in Madagascar

east_africa_presence: Orange Madagascar is one of the country's leading mobile network operators.
expansion_signal: Orange Madagascar renewed its comprehensive telecom license for ~€30 million (acquired December 2023) and is deploying 500 new 2G/3G sites via a 10-year partnership with NuRAN Wireless.
source_title: Orange Madagascar boosts telecom network coverage with new license and investments

east_africa_presence: Super U entered Madagascar's retail market by taking over Shoprite's 10-store supermarket network.
expansion_signal: Super U announced (reported September 2021) the takeover of Shoprite's 10 Madagascar stores, following Shoprite's exit from the market.
source_title: Super U takes over 10 Shoprite stores in Madagascar

east_africa_presence: Bolloré Logistics Malawi is the Malawi unit of the pan-African Bolloré Logistics freight-forwarding network.
expansion_signal: Won and completed the logistics contract for Malawi's 60MW Golomoti Solar project, shipping 221 TEUs via the Port of Beira between March and December 2021.
source_title: Bolloré Logistics Malawi successfully completes logistics for the Golomoti Solar project

east_africa_presence: Medine Group operates Cascavelle Shopping Mall in the island's western region, one of Mauritius's largest retail and leisure destinations.
expansion_signal: Announced a Rs 2.6 billion extension of Cascavelle Mall that will triple its footprint, adding 19,500m² and 66 new retail outlets, reported 18 July 2024.
source_title: Cascavelle Shopping Mall: Medine Group invests Rs 2.6 billion for extension

east_africa_presence: Emtel is Mauritius's first private mobile network operator.
expansion_signal: Launched Mauritius's first live 5G network (60% population coverage at launch) on 31 July 2023 and announced a BSS modernisation partnership with Tecnotree.
source_title: Emtel Mauritius launches 5G, taps Tecnotree for digital transformation

east_africa_presence: Eni operates the Coral Sul floating LNG facility off Mozambique's Rovuma Basin — the country's first LNG production.
expansion_signal: Coral Sul FLNG has been producing LNG since 2022, and Eni's approved Coral Norte development (3.55 million tonnes/year, production expected H2 2028) was cited as of August 2026.
source_title: Mozambique: Southern Africa's emerging industrial platform

hq: Ebene, Mauritius (backed by Africa Finance Corporation)
east_africa_presence: Pan-African industrial-zone developer; co-developing Rwanda's Bugesera Special Economic Zone (BSEZ) through joint venture BSEZ Ltd with the Government of Rwanda.
expansion_signal: Bank of Kigali ($33M) and Development Bank of Rwanda ($19M) injected a combined $52 million into the 335-hectare Bugesera Industrial Park/SEZ (part of a $100M project launched in 2023, Phase 1 of 75 hectares already operational), targeting light manufacturing, agro-processing, pharma and logistics tenants; reported August 2025.
source_title: BK, BRD Inject $52M into Bugesera Industrial Park

east_africa_presence: Regional manufacturer expanding into Rwanda; opened Rwanda's first-ever toothpaste factory inside the Kigali Special Economic Zone.
expansion_signal: Inaugurated Rwanda's first toothpaste factory ('ProSmile' brand) in Kigali Special Economic Zone, November 22, 2024.
source_title: FEATURED: RK Industries opens Rwanda's first toothpaste factory

hq: Paris, France (Groupe Duval); U Express is a Systeme U (France) supermarket brand
east_africa_presence: Developing Kigali's largest shopping mall (Inzovu Mall, Kimihurura) and bringing the French U Express supermarket chain into Rwanda as anchor tenant, with plans for 10 stores nationwide over 5 years.
expansion_signal: Construction of the $68-71M, 40,000 sqm Inzovu Mall began August 2023 (IFC and Proparco each providing $17.5M); first U Express store slated to open at the mall in early 2026, with completion/public opening late 2025.
source_title: Inzovu Mall developer, French supermarket chain to open 10 stores in Rwanda

company: AGL Rwanda (Africa Global Logistics, MSC Group)
hq: Marseille, France (AGL, part of the MSC Group)
east_africa_presence: Operates 21,000 sqm of bonded/duty-free warehousing across six sites in Rwanda's Kigali Special Economic Zone, a major freight-forwarding and customs logistics operator.
expansion_signal: Laid the foundation stone for a 5,000 sqm warehouse extension with cold-chain capability in the Kigali Special Economic Zone, April 15, 2024.
source_title: AGL Rwanda lays the foundation stone for the extension of its logistics warehouse in Kigali

hq: Kigali, Rwanda (pan-African regional body, backed by African Development Fund)
east_africa_presence: Rwanda-headquartered foundation established with Rwanda's Ministry of Health to build regional pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity and collective medicine procurement for Africa.
expansion_signal: African Development Fund board approved $12M financing for APTF's rapid operationalization in Kigali; financing approved February 2024, project launched in Kigali May 2024.
source_title: The $12M Regional Pharmaceutical Project Launched in Kigali

hq: Johannesburg, South Africa (Cassava Technologies, part of Econet Group)
east_africa_presence: Building its first data centre in Kigali as part of Cassava Technologies' $500 million plan to build 10 data centres across Africa, supporting Rwanda's digital transformation agenda.
expansion_signal: Broke ground on a purpose-built 2MW data centre in Kigali, Q1 2023.
source_title: Africa Data Centres to build its first data centre in Kigali, Rwanda

company: Thai Union Group (Indian Ocean Tuna Ltd)
east_africa_presence: Thai Union owns a majority (60%) stake in Indian Ocean Tuna Ltd, which operates one of the world's largest tuna canneries in Victoria, Seychelles.
expansion_signal: Thai Union announced a further EUR 10 million investment into the Seychelles cannery (on top of a prior EUR 40 million upgrade), announced late April/early May 2022.
source_title: Thai Union to invest another €10m in Seychelles tuna plant

east_africa_presence: Cable & Wireless Seychelles is one of the country's two main telecom/ISP operators.
expansion_signal: Inaugurated the 'Bon Espoir' Data Centre, Seychelles' first Tier IV data centre, unveiled 22 November 2024.
source_title: Cable & Wireless inaugurates state-of-the-art data centre

east_africa_presence: IFFCO, a Gulf-based FMCG/edible-oils conglomerate, entered Somaliland by signing a 25-year lease to build a large edible-oil packing plant inside DP World's Berbera Economic Zone.
expansion_signal: IFFCO announced construction of a 300,000 sq ft edible oil packing plant at the Berbera Economic Zone, announced 8 November 2022.
source_title: IFFCO to develop 300,000 square feet edible oil packing plant at DP World's Berbera Economic Zone, Somaliland

east_africa_presence: Hayat Market is a modern supermarket chain in Mogadishu operated by UAE-based Safa International Group.
expansion_signal: Since opening its first branch in April 2020, Hayat Market expanded to at least five branches across Mogadishu districts by 2025, named Best Supermarket Chain of the Year at the 2024 East Africa Somali Awards.
source_title: Hayat Market

east_africa_presence: Trinity Energy is a leading indigenous South Sudanese energy company operating fuel import, storage and distribution infrastructure.
expansion_signal: Advancing a planned USD 500 million, initially 60,000 bpd domestic oil refinery at Paloch, Upper Nile State; as of July 2024 had completed feasibility studies and secured land/concession.
source_title: South Sudan's Trinity Energy eyes domestic refinery despite local industry woes

east_africa_presence: Shandong Hi-Speed Group is a Chinese state-owned infrastructure conglomerate contracted for major South Sudanese highway construction.
expansion_signal: Signed/renewed a contract (announced 3 December 2020) to build the 392 km Juba-Rumbek highway, including 10 bridges, 35 box culverts and 21 viaducts.
source_title: South Sudan, Chinese firm renew contract for road construction

east_africa_presence: Tanzania-founded (2000) conglomerate with cement, construction, transport, flour and container-depot interests; expanding aggressively into Kenya (Bamburi Cement acquisition) and Zambia.
expansion_signal: Announced $320 million greenfield cement plant investment in Tanzania (1.6Mt/yr capacity), adding to its existing Camel Cement grinding plant and 65% stake in Mbeya Cement, November 2024.
source_title: Amsons Group takes aim at East Africa

east_africa_presence: Global port and logistics operator now managing key multi-purpose terminals at the Port of Dar es Salaam under a long-term concession, positioning Tanzania as a regional trade gateway for landlocked neighbours.
expansion_signal: Signed a 30-year concession with Tanzania Ports Authority to operate multi-purpose terminals at Dar es Salaam Port, with an initial investment exceeding $250M (potentially up to $1B across the concession, including hinterland logistics and a possible SEZ), October 22, 2023.
investment_as_disclosed: $250 million initial (up to $1 billion potential over 30-year term)
source_title: DP World Signs 30-Year Concession to Operate Multi-Purpose Dar es Salaam Port in Tanzania

east_africa_presence: Belt and Road-financed contractor executing Uganda's flagship Entebbe International Airport modernisation, alongside other Ugandan road and infrastructure contracts.
expansion_signal: Completed a new cargo terminal (doubling capacity to 100,000 tonnes/year) at Entebbe International Airport as part of a broader US$200 million airport modernisation programme (passenger terminal/runway work continuing into 2024).
source_title: China Communications delivers trade-boosting cargo terminal in Uganda

east_africa_presence: Contracted by the Ugandan government as main contractor for the Malaba-Kampala Standard Gauge Railway, its flagship Uganda infrastructure project.
expansion_signal: President Museveni launched construction of the 273km Malaba-Kampala Standard Gauge Railway (via Tororo, Jinja, Mukono etc.), expected complete within 48 months; groundbreaking November 21, 2024.
investment_as_disclosed: Project valued at ~UGX 10.8 trillion (~US$3 billion) per Ugandan government reporting
source_title: President Museveni Launches Construction Of Malaba-Kampala Standard Gauge Railway

east_africa_presence: Uganda's largest mobile network operator, part of the pan-African MTN Group footprint covering the wider East African region.
expansion_signal: Launched Uganda's first 5G network and industrial 5G use case, backed by a UGX 95.4 billion (~US$25.4 million) investment via its five-year Huawei modernisation partnership; live from early-to-May 2023.
source_title: MTN Uganda launches first 5G network, pioneering high-speed connectivity in the country

east_africa_presence: Operates the Shell-branded fuel retail network across Uganda alongside operations in over a dozen African markets.
expansion_signal: Commissioned 10 new Shell service stations (incl. Kitetika, Kitemu, Masanafu), bringing its Uganda network to 191 sites, and unveiled Shell's refreshed brand identity with MTN-partnered CCTV across all stations, November 2024.
source_title: Vivo Energy Expands Network With 10 New Service Stations, Unveils The New Look For Shell In Uganda

east_africa_presence: Operates the $450M Masaita cement plant near Ndola (1.5 Mt/yr capacity).
expansion_signal: Announced on 24 June 2024 it would double its Zambia investment to roughly $900M by building a second cement plant.
source_title: Dangote ramps up investment in Zambia with second plant

east_africa_presence: Zambian-listed property company that owns and operates retail malls in Lusaka.
expansion_signal: Completed a US$65 million acquisition of three Lusaka shopping malls (Acacia Park, Jacaranda Mall, Lewanika Mall) in November 2023.
source_title: REIZ Plc completes US$65mn acquisition of Zambia malls

east_africa_presence: Newly launched in-country Zambia operations offering freight forwarding, warehousing, transportation, customs brokerage and supply-chain management.
expansion_signal: Formally launched/rebranded its Zambia operations on 27 March 2024.
source_title: Africa Global Logistics has announced its launch in Zambia, which is set to transform the transport and logistics landscape in the region

company: West Property Group (with McCormick Property Development Group)
east_africa_presence: Zimbabwean property developer behind the Millennium City and Pokugara developments in Harare.
expansion_signal: Announced on 29 August 2024 a $100M 'Mall of Zimbabwe' project in Borrowdale, Harare, planned as the country's largest mall.
source_title: Construction of exquisite Mall of Zimbabwe to start Q2,2025

east_africa_presence: Zimbabwe-founded, ZSE-listed QSR operator (Chicken Inn, Pizza Inn, Creamy Inn) with its largest single-country network (332 outlets) in Zimbabwe.
expansion_signal: On 5 December 2024 announced plans to open 31 new outlets and refurbish 44 stores by fiscal year-end 2025.
source_title: Simbisa Brands to add 31 stores, exceeding 750 by fiscal year-end 2025
